description: Flat 8 m square of grey interlocking concrete block pavers in the Thai zigzag pattern -- one quad, one seamless PBR texture set, tiling in both axes.

image.prompt:
A SEAMLESSLY TILING TOP-DOWN GROUND TEXTURE. This is a flat material swatch, not a photograph of a scene or of an object. The camera looks straight down at the ground from directly overhead, perfectly orthographic, with no perspective, no horizon, no vanishing point and no tilt.

The surface: Flat square of interlocking concrete block paving seen as a single unbroken surface, identical S-curved zigzag blocks locked together in straight courses with fine tight joints, a few blocks a shade lighter or darker than their neighbours, edge to edge blocks only, no kerb and no border Materials: Seamlessly tiling mid-grey precast concrete pavers with a slightly rough sand-cement face, mould-sharp chamfered top edges catching light, tonal drift block to block from pale grey to charcoal, fine pale sand swept into the joints with weeds in a few, dark oil spotting and tyre scuffs, sun-bleached patches and damp grey staining, a few chipped corners and one or two blocks sunk slightly below their neighbours; the block layout must wrap on all four edges so a run of tiles gives unbroken continuous courses.

Scale: the square shown covers exactly 8 by 8 metres of real ground, so every stone, block, slab, joint, marking, rut and tuft in it is drawn at its true size relative to that. Do not zoom in on a detail and do not pull back to show a wider scene.

Tiling: the texture must repeat seamlessly on all four edges. What runs off the left edge continues onto the right edge, and what runs off the top continues onto the bottom, exactly. No feature may be cut in half at an edge without its other half appearing at the opposite edge. Laid out four by four this must read as one continuous surface with no visible grid, no repeated landmark feature and no seam.

Framing: the surface fills the entire frame edge to edge and corner to corner. There is no border, no frame, no margin, no backdrop, no background, no matte and no empty space of any kind. The ground continues past every edge of the image.

Nothing stands on it and nothing bounds it: no kerb, no wall, no step, no gutter, no drain, no manhole cover, no grass verge, no plants, no people, no vehicles, no furniture, no objects, no litter, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows.

Lighting: flat, even, shadowless overhead illumination, like a lightbox. The image is the surface's true albedo. No sun, no cast shadows, no directional highlights, no specular blowout, no vignette, no gradient across the frame, no baked ambient occlusion in the corners and crevices, no light falloff towards the edges -- an uneven frame cannot tile, because its bright side would meet its dark side at every seam.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, realistic material, real surface wear and staining. Not stylised, not cartoon, not a 3D render preview, not a tiled collage of separate photographs, not a pattern illustration.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Whole-asset visual estimate 96/100 for the current prescribed single-quad interlocking concrete tile at intended game distance. Measured 2/2 triangles, 1/1 draw, 1/1 material, 1/1 geometry. Three 1024 maps use 16 MiB estimated GPU memory. Packed ORM and ordinary PBR channels pass actual editor export and decoded pixel checks. PBR extractor reports .813 with a weak full-frame mask; production full-frame fields were separately inspected. Physical microheight remains inferred. Baseline 86 and overstrong-rim draft 93 remain in review history.

featureReviews.notes: Aligned 0/180 degree grid has no geometric gaps or dominant alternating light/dark blocks. Neutral normal borders and corrected field boundaries restrain seams. Minor inherited course cuts and repeated repairs remain at magnification; an exact synthesized block tessellation is not claimed.

name: Interlocking Concrete Paver Tile
nameTh: พื้นอิฐตัวหนอน
notes: One flat quad, 8 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. The entire surface reads out of the texture; not a single paver is modelled, and the chamfered block edges are carried by the normal and AO maps. This is the everyday Thai ground surface and the workhorse of the kit's ground-surface tile set -- sidewalks, shop forecourts, petrol station aprons, car parks, temple approaches, condo entrances are all this block, known locally as the worm brick -- so it will be instanced more heavily than any other ground tile and one shared geometry with one shared material is what lets an InstancedMesh collapse a whole plaza. Every tile in the ground set is 8 x 8 m, sits at y=0, uses pivot base-center and snaps on the kit's 8 m grid, so it butts flush against any other ground tile and against the asphalt road tiles, and the raised Concrete Sidewalk Strip (2.0 m wide, 0.15 m tall) sits alongside as a separate object. The blocks are laid in COURSES, so unlike an irregular paving this tile is only TWO-way rotationally symmetric: it drops in at 0 or 180 degrees, and a 90 degree rotation deliberately turns the courses across the run, which is a real thing builders do at a change of area and is worth having rather than hiding. The course pitch must divide 8 m evenly and wrap at all four edges, or every tile boundary shows a half block -- that is the first thing to check on the generated texture. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. One risk specific to this tile: a flat mid-grey concrete surface can land close to the reference plate's grey backdrop and confuse a silhouette gate, so the generated plate wants tonal variation block to block rather than one even grey. No destruction groups: a ground tile is static level geometry, not a breakable. Quality refinement: separate Patina basecolor, normal and packed AO/roughness now ship as three maps. Normal strength .18 and local height-derived joint AO .6 balance chamfers and recesses; original glossy roughness is corrected for dry concrete. Eight img2threejs scopes accepted at visual estimate 96 after two corrections. Installed 12-view parity and actual editor GLB pixels verified. One quad, root pivot and ground-aligned collision slab retained. The .813 extraction heuristic masks mostly joints, so its full-face colour inference is not used. Reference course cuts remain; physical depth is inferred. Evidence: scratch/interlocking-concrete-paver-tile/quality-above95/round02.
